R7RS-small 4.1.4: (lambda args args) takes any number of arguments as a list; Lion's lambda takes only a list of parameters, so ["lambda", "args", "args"] is not well-formed. Library functions already take any number after the ones they need, as array/make and func/partial do, so a rest parameter would follow the arity rule. Waits for the user; recommended: build a rest parameter for lambda.

R7RS-small 4.2.1: (and) is #t; Lion refuses ["and"] as not well-formed, as a goal. Waits for the user; recommended: fix, so that ["and"] is true and ["or"] is false, the empty conjunction and disjunction, in plain code and as goals.
R7RS-small 4.2.1: (or) is #f; Lion refuses ["or"] as not well-formed. Waits for the user; recommended: fix it with and-no-arguments.

R7RS-small 4.2.1: and gives the value of its last expression, as (and 1 2) is 2; Lion's and takes only booleans and goals, the rule names-by-scope states for cond, whose cond-zero-condition and like cases are already excepted. Waits for the user; recommended: except it, with or-gives-first-true-value and not-of-non-boolean, in a decision that a condition is a boolean in and, or, not, and boolean/not as it is in cond.

R7RS-small 4.2.1: or gives the first value that is not #f, as (or #f 3) is 3; Lion's or takes only booleans and goals. Waits for the user; recommended: except it with and-gives-last-value, since conditions are booleans.

R7RS-small 6.3: (not 3) is #f, since every value but #f is true; boolean/not, like the not form, takes only a boolean. Waits for the user; recommended: except it with and-gives-last-value, since conditions are booleans.

R7RS-small 4.2.1: a cond clause's body is one or more expressions, and the clause gives the last one's value; Lion's case is a condition and one result. Waits for the user; recommended: except it, since a result written with begin does the same and one result keeps every case a pair, as the analysis and the editor read it.

R7RS-small 4.2.5: the report's example forces a promise inside its own force and gives 6; Lion fails, as Racket's force does with a reentrant promise, and the delay-and-force record says Lion's delay is Racket's. Waits for the user; recommended: except it, naming Racket as the precedent.

R7RS-small 4.2.7: guard gives its handler the raised object itself, as Racket's with-handlers does; func/catch gives a record {failure, message, value}, so one handler reads every failure the same way, as catchable-failures chose. Waits for the user; recommended: except it by that decision.

R7RS-small 5.5: a record's modifier changes the record; Lion's records are JSON values, and object/set gives a new record, as Racket's immutable hash-set does. Waits for the user; recommended: except it, since values are immutable data that facts and answers can hold.

R7RS-small 6.2.6: (+) is 0; number/add takes one or more, while the README says the six combining functions work as +, *, min, max, string-append, and append do in Scheme, and Scheme's take zero or more for all but min and max. Waits for the user; recommended: fix, so that number/add, number/multiply, array/concat, and string/concat take zero or more and give 0, 1, [], and "" for none.
R7RS-small 6.2.6: (*) is 1; number/multiply takes one or more. Waits for the user; recommended: fix it with add-no-arguments.
R7RS-small 6.4: (append) is the empty list; array/concat takes one or more. Waits for the user; recommended: fix it with add-no-arguments.
R7RS-small 6.7: (string-append) is the empty string; string/concat takes one or more. Waits for the user; recommended: fix it with add-no-arguments.

R7RS-small 6.4: taking the car of the empty list is an error, which Racket signals; array/head of [] gives null, which cannot be told from the head of [null]. Waits for the user; recommended: fix, so that array/head and array/tail of [] fail as car and cdr do.
R7RS-small 6.4: taking the cdr of the empty list is an error; array/tail of [] gives []. Waits for the user; recommended: fix it with car-of-empty-list.

R7RS-small 6.7: a string is a sequence of characters, so (string-length "𝄞") is 1; string/length counts UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript does, and so do string/slice, string/indexOf, and string/split. R7RS-small 6.10: (apply + (list 3 4)) is 7; func/apply takes a this-object and passes the arguments after it as they are, as JavaScript's call does, so it spreads no list, unlike Scheme's apply and JavaScript's own Function.prototype.apply.
